purpose: The ONE registry of AgentNet's desired product state for the Maintenance OS (ADR-0010 D2). Each contract names the SLIs it feeds, the trusted detectors that observe it, the trusted tests that judge a repair of it, and what an autonomous repair may never touch. This file, every detector and every verification test named here are TRUSTED EVALUATION CRITERIA: a repair candidate that edits them together with the product is evaluation laundering and is classified RED (policy.py).

contracts.description: Every public page and API endpoint in the public-surface contract answers with the contracted status, final path and markers.

Critical pages render readable, navigable, accessible content in a real browser: no console/JS errors, no failed same-origin requests, no dead navigation, WCAG 2.2 AA text contrast, labelled form fields, human-readable capability badges (never a raw structured value), no unexpected error banner on a successful page, no horizontal overflow.
The public API is healthy and ready (health, readiness, no 5xx on contracted endpoints).
The A2A 1.0 Agent Card is served, protocol version and bindings match ADR-0009, official SDK clients interoperate, tenants stay isolated.
Anonymous register and login pages render and post to the API; redirects terminate; verification email health is signalled by a bounded canary, never one account per probe.
Transactional email is accepted by the provider for the verification flow.

Wallet balances change only through triggers; escrow is reserved/released/refunded exactly once; platform fee math holds. A violation FREEZES mutations and escalates as P0; an autonomous repair never rewrites balances or data.

Rate limiting keys by the vouched peer (B1), /metrics exposes no request paths (X1), CORS admits only the canonical origin, session cookies are secure, every mutating route rejects anonymous callers, no secret is committed.
Critical public pages stay within document/resource size and third-party budgets; a regression must be sustained across repeated runs before it is an incident.
Every service requirement set passes pip-audit (documented exceptions only), dependency graphs resolve coherently, runtimes are supported. Major upgrades are never automatic.
